title: Term list vocabulary
description: Words, patterns and heading rules about the meaning of text, grouped by domain and labelled. A term list is `sys.trm.<scope>.<domain>` and lives at `seed/terms/<scope>/<domain>.yml`; the scope is `global` or a country, chosen by where the meaning is true, not where the word was found. Language is a tag on each term, never a scope. Terms are neutral: they never name a table. A column dictionary (`sys.col.<scope>.<domain>`) or a mapping links database columns to groups and patterns here by list code and key. Groups with the same key merge across the lists a consumer loads, and terms with the same value merge their aliases.

extends.description: Codes of term lists this one builds on. Each must be in this list's scope or global; a global list extends none.

languages.description: Language codes (reference.languages codes such as en, sw) the list's terms are written in. A term or alias without its own language takes the first one.

terms.description: Terms that belong to no group. Use groups for anything a ranking rule will refer to.

group.description: The group's key. Groups with this key in other loaded lists are the same group.

role.description: How consumers use the group: kind (what a document is), subject (what it is about), stopword (ignored when tokenising) or concept (general vocabulary a column dictionary or pattern refers to; the default).

shape.description: What the cells under a heading matching this group look like; evidence for the column matcher.

kind_words.description: The words only say what kind of thing a name is (county, town, limited). The lookup drops them from a name key and reads them as evidence of the record's kind.

group.description: A named, labelled set of terms. In a column list it is one database column (target), or one value of a controlled scheme (member); in a document list it is a kind or subject.

value.description: The canonical term. Matches of any alias count as this term.

kind.description: concept: a word for a kind of thing (county, governor). instance: a named thing (Kiambu, IEBC); prefer a refers_to link or the seed data. abbreviation. title: a form of address or office. unit: currency, measure or scale. pattern-word: only meaningful inside a pattern.

represents.description: The reference value or seed row this term stands for in the real world, for example geo.feature.kind.county or fin.currency.kes. A global term may not represent a country-scoped code.

variant_of.description: The value of another term in this list that this is a form of: MP is a variant of member of parliament; gavana (sw) of governor. Prefer an alias for plain spelling or language variants; use variant_of when the form has its own meaning or register.

refers_to.description: For an instance: the seed row it names. Add it only when the word is not already a name or alias in the data.

applies_to.description: Countries where a global term has this meaning, when it does not hold everywhere.

source.description: The publisher or document family the usage comes from, for wording specific to one source.

key.description: A key: lowercase words joined by dashes. Groups, patterns, heading rules and splits are addressed as <list code> plus key.

part.description: One part of a pattern, in order. Exactly one of group, literal, words, digits, letters, punct, any_of.

as.description: Name of the capture this part fills.

group.description: A word or phrase from a group: <key> in this list, or <list code>#<key> from another.

words.description: A word of letters in this case style.

punct.description: Any of these punctuation characters, such as .,-/

number.description: A number as written in documents: digits with optional thousands separators and decimals (1,200,000.50). Captured as the written text.

lazy.description: With repeat: take as few as possible, so a following part can claim the rest (a landmark name before the word Road).

captures.description: The values the pattern must capture; checked when the term files are tested.

means.description: What a match is: person, organisation, role, place, address, money, date, phone, reference.

sequences.description: The orders in which the parts may occur; each sequence is one allowed order.

examples.description: Texts that must match. They run as tests.

counterexamples.description: Texts that must not match. They run as tests.

qualifier_is.description: What the part of the heading in brackets or after a dash says. The base is matched to a column; the qualifier is read as a unit, an abbreviation marker, a date format and so on.

sequences.description: Use captures named base and qualifier.

heading_rule.description: The heading rule (key, or <list code>#<key>) the heading must match.

cell_pattern.description: The pattern (key, or <list code>#<key>) most cells must match.

min_share.description: Share of sampled cells that must match before the column is proposed as two.
